lesson_topic: The Cold War — Origins: Capitalism vs. Communism Ideological Foundations

principles.evidence: All four slides contain exclusively text-based content with no diagrams, charts, maps, illustrations, or data figures present in either the visual or narration channel. The absence of any non-decorative graphic across every slide means reciprocity between visual and verbal channels cannot be established.

On-screen text consists of full, multi-sentence paragraphs on every slide, far exceeding the keyword-and-label standard. The transcript narration is verbatim — or near-verbatim — reproduction of the on-screen prose, providing zero substantive elaboration beyond what is already displayed.

Complex descriptive content is delivered entirely through dense on-screen text rather than narration over supportive graphics, violating the core modality prescription. The narration reads the on-screen paragraph text aloud verbatim while no visual is present, placing the full cognitive load simultaneously on both written and auditory verbal channels.

No decorative imagery, tangential anecdotes, or off-topic filler content is present in either channel; all text content is topically relevant to the stated learning objectives. Styling and font treatment appear consistent across slides, though the absence of graphics limits assessment of visual coherence to typographic elements only.

No visual cues such as arrows, highlights, bold emphasis, or callouts are employed to mark key elements on any slide; a basic title hierarchy is present but constitutes the sole organizational signal. The narration contains no verbal signaling language directing learner attention to specific concepts or takeaways.

Because no graphics are present, split-attention conditions between text and visuals cannot arise; all text elements are internally co-located and no legend-body separation exists. Spatial contiguity criteria are trivially satisfied by the text-only layout but cannot be meaningfully assessed without visual-verbal pairings.
